title: Is He the One? A Christian Discernment Profile
subtitle: Honest questions for the decision you keep praying about.

questions.text: When you picture a hard season five years in, how does he show up?

options.text: Steady. He's already shown me he stays when things get heavy.
I think he'd stay, but I haven't really seen it tested yet.
Honestly, he checks out the second things get uncomfortable.
I can't picture it clearly because we're both still so unformed.

questions.text: How does his faith actually look on a normal Tuesday?

options.text: Real and his own. It shapes how he treats people, not just Sundays.
Sincere but young. He's growing, and I'm watching the direction.
He talks the language but the fruit isn't there.
We're both kind of rebuilding our faith from scratch right now.

questions.text: When you bring up a concern, what happens?

options.text: He listens, owns his part, and we come out closer.
It's hit or miss. Sometimes great, sometimes he gets defensive.
It gets turned around on me until I'm the one apologizing.
We both shut down. Neither of us has learned to do conflict well yet.

questions.text: What do the wise people in your life say when they see you two?

options.text: They light up. They've told me unprompted that he's good for me.
They're cautiously hopeful and keep saying "give it time."
The people who love me most are quietly worried.
They mostly say we're both a bit too unsettled to know yet.

questions.text: How safe do you feel being fully yourself around him?

options.text: Completely. I'm more me with him, not less.
Mostly, though I still hold a few things back to keep the peace.
I shrink. I've started editing myself to avoid his reactions.
I'm honestly still figuring out who "fully myself" even is.

questions.text: Be honest about why you're asking if he's the one:

options.text: Because everything good in me wants to build a life with him.
Because it's mostly good and I want to make sure before I go all in.
Because I'm trying to talk myself into staying.
Because I want this to work eventually, but the timing feels off.

questions.text: Is there anything in the relationship that scares you?

options.text: Only the normal fear that comes with loving someone this much.
A couple of patterns I want to watch a little longer.
Yes. There's a fear I keep explaining away, and I shouldn't.
Mostly I'm scared we're both not ready, not that he's wrong.

questions.text: When you pray about him, what's the honest sense you keep getting?

options.text: Peace. A settled yes I can't shake.
"Keep going, but stay awake."
A pull in my gut I keep arguing with.
"Not now. Grow first."

questions.text: How does he treat the people who can do nothing for him?

options.text: With real kindness. It's the same whether anyone's watching or not.
Usually well, though I've seen a couple of moments that gave me pause.
Differently than he treats me, and it worries me.
He's still maturing in that, same as I am.

questions.text: If a friend described your exact situation to you, you'd tell her...

options.text: "Don't overthink a good thing. This one's worth it."
"Take your time and keep your eyes open."
"Friend, you already know. It's time to walk away."
"You two aren't ready yet, and that's okay. Keep growing."

green-light-pursue.name: Green Light: Pursue
green-light-pursue.description: The evidence keeps pointing the same direction. He's steady, his faith is real, and you're more yourself around him, not less. There's no such thing as a perfect person, so don't wait for one. Pursue this with open eyes and a grateful heart.

scripture.text: He who finds a wife finds what is good and receives favor from the Lord.

yellow-pray-and-watch.name: Yellow: Pray and Watch
yellow-pray-and-watch.description: There's a lot of good here, and a few things you genuinely need to see play out. That's not a no. It's a slow yes that hasn't earned your whole heart yet. Keep praying, keep your eyes open, and give time the chance to show you what words can't.

scripture.text: The simple believe anything, but the prudent give thought to their steps.

red-walk-away.name: Red: Walk Away
red-walk-away.description: You keep explaining away something your gut already flagged. The fact that you're working this hard to stay is the answer. Walking away from the wrong thing isn't a failure of faith. It's how you stay available for the right one. You're allowed to choose peace.

scripture.text: Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

not-yet-keep-growing.name: Not Yet: Keep Growing
not-yet-keep-growing.description: The problem here probably isn't him. It's the timing. You're both still becoming who you'll be, and a healthy thing planted in unready soil can struggle for no good reason. Keep growing your own roots. If it's right, it can wait for you to be ready.

scripture.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.
